questions.stem: Which of the following is a primitive type in most programming languages?
questions.explanation: Integer is a primitive type commonly found in programming languages, used to represent whole numbers.

distractorRationale.a: Strings are not primitive types; they are typically objects or arrays of characters.
distractorRationale.c: Arrays are not primitive types; they are collections of elements.
distractorRationale.d: Objects are not primitive types; they are instances of classes.

questions.stem: What is the result of adding 1 to the maximum value of a 32-bit signed integer?

distractorRationale.b: 1 is incorrect; it would be the result if there were no overflow.
distractorRationale.d: 2,147,483,648 is incorrect; it exceeds the range of a 32-bit signed integer.

questions.stem: Explain why floating-point arithmetic can lead to precision errors. Use an example to illustrate your explanation.
markingGuide: Explanation of binary representation of floating-point numbers.

questions.stem: Describe the difference between integer and floating-point division, and provide an example to illustrate.
markingGuide: Explanation of integer division resulting in a whole number.
Explanation of floating-point division allowing fractional results.
Example comparing integer division and floating-point division.
